note.question: Should an online service platform set one common price or let privately informed providers set their own prices, and what fee schedule preserves decentralized autonomy while optimally regulating competition?
note.overview: A platform commits to a pricing regime and fee schedule while a continuum of privately informed agents strategically chooses participation and, under decentralization, prices. The paper defines a nonatomic price equilibrium, solves centralized and decentralized regimes, and designs incentive-compatible fees that implement the platform-optimal allocation.

components.label: Unique nonatomic price equilibrium under price-affine fees with truth-inducing optimal mechanism implementations
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Unique nonatomic price equilibrium under price-affine fees with truth-inducing optimal mechanism implementations. A price profile is an equilibrium when every active agent's price maximizes that agent's profit given the resulting average price and participation cutoff. Proposition 2 proves uniqueness only for price-affine fees. Proposition 5 gives the truth-inducing direct optimum, and Propositions 6-7 identify unique optimal commission-plus and quantity-based fee parameterizations that implement the same allocation and payoffs.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The platform first announces who controls prices, the fee structure, and under centralized pricing the common price. Agents then observe the policy and their own private costs, decide whether to participate, and under decentralized pricing choose posted prices while correctly anticipating the aggregate market price. Customers receive service, revenue is earned, and the platform collects fees. The platform moves first by selecting price control and payment rules.

components.label: Objective and constraints
components.explanation: The platform chooses an allocation-price schedule and per-unit fee schedule to maximize total fee revenue subject to truth-telling, participation, and aggregate-price consistency; each decentralized agent in turn prices to maximize its own demand times net unit margin.
